Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the second essay as the umpires make their way out to the middle. The New Zealand players are in a huddle at the boundary line for a few last-minute instructions from Tim Southee before taking their respective positions on the field. Muhammad Waseem and Aryansh Sharma will open the inning for United Arab Emirates and will want to get a good partnership going here. Tim Southee has the new ball in his hand and is ready to begin proceedings. Let's go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

The game could have ended differently had Mitchell Santner not survived a caught behind appeal as the umpire missed seeing him glove the ball to the keeper. He scored a quickfire 20 to push his side to a competitive total and United Arab Emirates will feel hard done by the decision. Junaid Siddique stood out for the hosts as he claimed three crucial wickets in his quota of 4 overs and conceded just 26 runs. Muhammad Jawadullah and Zahoor Khan chipped in with one wicket each but the spinners had very little impact in this game. Will New Zealand's bowlers rise to the occasion and quell UAE's batting onslaught, or will the hosts etch their name in history? Do join us shortly to see how the second innings pans out.

In a pivotal decider game of the series, New Zealand has posted a total of 166 runs in their first innings having been put in to bat first. They will be happy with the score as this is the highest they have achieved in this series and they will be silently confident of defending this target. The early stages of New Zealand's innings saw them lose two wickets inside the Powerplay. However, the duo of Will Young and Mark Chapman emerged as the saviours, scripting an impressive recovery with an 84-run partnership for the third wicket. Will Young's exquisite 56 off 46 balls set the tone before he departed followed by Mark Chapman who contributed with a rapid 51 off 32 balls embellished with 5 boundaries and 2 towering sixes.

Commentary.Commentary: The umpires are out in the middle as the match is about to begin. The United Arab Emirates have taken their respective positions on the field as Tim Seifert and Chad Bowes stride out to the centre to open the innings for New Zealand. They will be hoping for a good start and will face Muhammad Jawadullah who has the new ball in his hand as he waits to begin proceedings. Let's play...

PITCH REPORT - Mitchell McClenaghan is pitchside and he says that the wicket looks hard so it will be good for batting. Mentions that there is some grass on the wicket which is holding it together and the ball is not going to stay as low as it did in the previous game. Ends by saying that we can expect a good score in the first innings on this wicket.

Tim Southee, the captain of New Zealand says that they will look to go for partnerships and will look to put a good score on the board. He informs that they have made three changes to the side and will look to play their best game in the series decider game tonight.

Muhammad Waseem, skipper of United Arab Emirates says that the plan is very simple as they will look to chase again and it looks like a good wicket to bat on. He adds that the boys are prepared and will look to execute their plans to perfection.

United Arab Emirates (Playing XI) - Muhammad Waseem (C), Aryansh Sharma (WK), Vriitya Aravind, Asif Khan, Ansh Tandon, Basil Hameed, Aayan Khan, Mohammed Faraazuddin, Muhammad Jawadullah, Junaid Siddique (In place of Ali Naseer), Zahoor Khan.

New Zealand (Playing XI) - Tim Seifert (WK), Chad Bowes, Will Young (In place of James Neesham), Mark Chapman, Dean Foxcroft (In place of Dane Cleaver), Mitchell Santner, Rachin Ravindra, Kyle Jamieson, Tim Southee (C), Adithya Ashok (In place of Cole McConchie), Benjamin Lister.
TOSS - The captains are out in the middle. The coin is flipped into the air and lands in favour of United Arab Emirates. They have elected to BOWL first.

United Arab Emirates will be on the moon with what they have managed to achieve and the credit falls heavily on their bowlers who have been on song throughout this series. the young Aayan Khan was the star with the ball in the last match claiming a three-wicket haul and conceding just 20 runs. Junaid Siddique missed the last game but Muhammad Jawadullah came in his stead and bowled brilliantly to claim two wiclets. Muhammad Waseem, the captain of United Arab Emirates was dismissed on a golden duck in the first game and he made amends with a quickfire half-century to set up his side's win. Will they be able to pull off yet another coup? Or will New Zealand come roaring back? We will find out soon. Stay tuned as we bring you the toss and team updates.

New Zealand have been poor with the bat so far in this series having scored sub-par scores in both the matches so far. Tim Seifert and Mark Chapman are the only two batters who have made any substantial contributions with both notching up a half-century in the two encounters. They were bailed out by their bowlers in the first match with Tim Southee claiming a five-wicket haul but their opponents managed to hold their nerves in the last match and get over the finish line. This defeat will not sit well with the management who have rested some senior players in order to help plan for the upcoming Cricket World Cup in India later this year. We expect the Kiwis to come back stronger in this match and are still favourites to clinch the series despite the hiccup.

Hello, and a warm welcome, ladies and gentlemen to our coverage of the third and final game in this 3-match T20I series between United Arab Emirates and New Zealand from the Dubai International Cricket Stadium where we are about to witness a memorable contest between one of the giants of international cricket and a giant killer. This series has all the makings of a Bollywood script as New Zealand suffered their first defeat against a non-Test playing nation in 39 encounters across formats in their last game. It was the host's first T20I win in Dubai in their eighth attempt and they are now in a position to seal their first-ever international series win so fasten your seatbelts for a cracking game.
... MATCH DAY ...

It is now time for the third and final T20I of the historic T20I series between the United Arab Emirates and New Zealand. Before a ball was bowled in the series, not many would have thought that we would be witnessing a decider, but such has been the fight shown by this spirited United Arab Emirates side. After New Zealand successfully managed to survive a scare in the first T20I, the hosts outplayed the visitors in all three departments in the second T20I and levelled the series. Trailing by a 1-0 deficit, the United Arab Emirates bowlers, especially young left-arm spinner Aayan Khan, picked up where they left off in the first T20I and kept New Zealand in check. In reply, skipper Muhammad Waseem scored an entertaining fifty before Asif Khan, with his blistering cameo, took the hosts over the line with more than four overs to spare. For the United Arab Emirates, their openers Muhammad Waseem and Aryansh Sharma have notched up crucial fifties, while Vriitya Aravind and Asif Khan have shown glimpses of what they can do with the bat. In the spin department, Aayan Khan has stood out, and he has been well supported by Mohammed Faraazuddin and Basil Hameed. When it comes to the pace department, Muhammad Jawadullah was impressive in the second T20I, but he will have to be complemented by Ali Naseer and Zahoor Khan. As far as New Zealand are concerned, they have been let down by their batters, who are yet to adjust to the pace and bounce of the surface at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium. With not much turnaround time between the second and third T20I, the likes of Tim Seifert, Mark Chapman, and James Neesham will have to bring their experience into play. Coming to the bowling unit, Tim Southee has truly led from the front with wickets in the powerplay in both games. Kyle Jamieson has not been that effective on his return, but it has been made up for by decent performances from Mitchell Santner and James Neesham. Will New Zealand take their game up a notch and clinch the series? Or will the United Arab Emirates punch above their weight again? We will find out soon enough.
